en: Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for its perfect cone shape and is the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle is the national bird and is endemic to the dense forests of the island of Mindanao.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an 8-kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a freshwater lake situated within a volcanic caldera and contains Volcano Island in its center.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest peak in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected UNESCO World Heritage site known for pristine coral atolls.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley in Luzon.
Luzon is the largest and most populous island in the Philippine archipelago, containing the national capital region of Manila.
The Tamaraw, a small hoofed mammal related to the water buffalo, is critically endangered and found only on Mindoro island.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by the indigenous Ifugao people over 2,000 years ago.
The Visayan Sea is a small inland sea located in the central Philippines, surrounded by the islands of Luzon, Mindanao, and Visayas.
White Beach in Boracay, Aklan, is a four-kilometer-long stretch of fine white coral sand famous for its stunning sunset views.
